classification.difficultyReason: The student must reject a plausible misconception (the display stops, so the decimal terminates) and explain using irrational, non-terminating, non-recurring ideas. The only digits shown are a calculator display, so there is no digit list to inspect as with pi. It is one conceptual explanation with no multi-step calculation, so it sits slightly above the pi classification.

content.prompt: A calculator displays $\sqrt{2}$ as $1.414213562$. A student says this is a terminating decimal because the display stops. Is the student correct? Explain your reasoning.

answer.short: No. The display shows only 9 decimal places, rounded. The true decimal never ends and does not repeat, so it is neither terminating nor recurring.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\sqrt{2}&=1.414213562\,37\ldots\\\text{Display}&=1.414213562\quad(9\text{ decimal places})\end{align*}$$The calculator stops because its screen is limited, not because the decimal ends. The digits continue forever with no repeating block, so $\sqrt{2}$ is neither terminating nor recurring. The student is not correct.
